newsitem.title: USA: SQUASH-JANSHER MOVES A STEP CLOSER TO CAREER AMBITION.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-JANSHER MOVES A STEP CLOSER TO CAREER AMBITION.

text.p: Jansher Khan, the top-seeded defending champion, won his eighth World Open title on Friday, beating second seed Rodney Eyles of Australia 15-13 17-15 11-15 15-3.

The win took Jansher one step closer to his career ambition of winning 10 World Open titles and six British Open championships to reverse the record of his great Pakistani predecessor Jahangir Khan who won the world title six times and the British event 10 times.
"Actually I think I can win 11 or 12 World Opens if I play to about 32 as I plan to," Jansher said.
"I did not play as well today as I did earlier in the tournament. I think playing in front of my home crowd with the world title at stake made me more nervous than usual."
In the opening two games the Pakistani looked tense and was never more than a point ahead of his rival until he took a 9-7 lead in the second game.
Even then Eyles was unlucky not to clinch the game when he fought back from 9-13 down to lead 14-13 only to have a let called on what might have been a crucial winning shot.
"I found the pace in that period," Eyles said afterwards. "I went on to win the third fairly easily playing the same way."
But despite the Australian's good work in the third, Jansher regained control in the fourth, taking seven successive points to establish a lead from which Eyles never recovered.
While it was not a vintage performance from Jansher, the result confirmed his status as the undisputed ruler of world squash.
"I have beaten him twice, once from behind and once from in front," Eyles reflected. "I am at the frustrating stage now of never being far enough away from him but not often enough on top."

Only Jahangir, who won two amateur world titles as well as his six World Open championships, and Australia's Geoff Hunt, with four World Opens and three amateur titles, come close to Jansher's achievements.
